question.value: Can massive planets explain the different continuum and CO morphology within LkCa 15’s dust cavity, and what constraints follow on their masses?

evidence.quote: Our main goal is to investigate if the different morphology of continuum and CO emission observed within LkCa 15’s disk dust cavity might be consistent with the presence of massive planets and derive constraints on their mass if this is the case.
The first observations were obtained as part of ALMA Cycle 6 in July 2019 (Project ID:2018.1.00350.S) in an extended configuration with baselines ranging from 91 m to 8.5 km.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.01123.L.
We analyze ALMA Band 7 data of LkCa 15 taken at two different epochs.

analysis_steps.goal: Initialize the disk and calculate its temperature

method.value: Initialize the α-disk surface-density profile; construct vertical gas/dust distributions; iterate RADMC3D temperature and aspect ratio to hydrostatic convergence.

evidence.quote: Following the evolution of an $\alpha$ disk (cite: Lynden-Bell+1974; Pringle+1981; Hartmann+1998; Isella+2009), we assume an initial gas surface density profile
The vertical gas density profile is calculated assuming that the disk is vertically isothermal and in hydrostatic equilibrium

To find the disk temperature profile corresponding to the hydrostatic equilibrium, we start from an initial guess of the disk aspect ratio and iterate on the temperature calculated by RADMC3D until convergence.
